what: McKesson distributes prescription medicines. It buys drugs from manufacturers and delivers them to pharmacies, hospitals and doctors' offices across North America, and runs specialty services around cancer care and prescription technology.
customers: Retail and independent pharmacies, hospital systems, oncology practices and pharmaceutical manufacturers.
money: distributing branded, generic and specialty drugs
practice services and distribution for cancer and specialty care
software linking manufacturers, pharmacies and patients
medical supplies to clinics and doctors' offices
moat: Three distributors handle almost all US drug volume. The scale of the warehouse and delivery network, and contracts with large pharmacy chains, make entry impractical.
risks: Margins are very thin: about one cent of profit on each dollar of revenue
Losing or repricing a single large pharmacy contract moves results materially
Opioid litigation settlements still require payments over many years
Government action on drug pricing changes how distributors are paid
opportunities: Specialty and oncology drugs carry better economics than ordinary distribution
GLP-1 weight-loss drugs push large volumes through the network
Steady cash flow funds continuous share buybacks, which lift earnings per share
watch: Operating profit by segment rather than revenue, since revenue is dominated by pass-through drug cost.
